beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: People have always wondered how prayer really works. Do you have to say it just right? Wear God down? Jesus, teaching on a hillside, made it startlingly simple.

timing.text: People have always wondered how prayer really works.

beats.speaker: jesus
beats.text: Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you:

timing.text: Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you:

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Three words, and each one is warmer and more personal than the last. Ask — like a child who simply puts out its hands, trusting, expecting good.

timing.text: Three words, and each one is warmer and more personal than the last.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Seek — more than a word now; it is getting up and searching, patient and hopeful, sure that what you are looking for is really there to be found.

timing.text: Seek — more than a word now; it is getting up and searching, patient and hopeful, sure that what you are looking for is really there to be found.

beats.speaker: jesus
beats.text: For every one that asketh receiveth; and he that seeketh findeth; and to him that knocketh it shall be opened.

timing.text: For every one that asketh receiveth; and he that seeketh findeth; and to him that knocketh it shall be opened.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Knock — and keep knocking — on a door you cannot yet see behind. And the promise is that the door does open. Not maybe. Not for the specially worthy. Every one who asks, receives.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Then Jesus makes it personal with a picture from any home.

timing.text: Then Jesus makes it personal with a picture from any home.

beats.speaker: jesus
beats.text: Or what man is there of you, whom if his son ask bread, will he give him a stone? Or if he ask a fish, will he give him a serpent?

timing.text: Or what man is there of you, whom if his son ask bread, will he give him a stone?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A child asks its father for bread. What kind of father hands his hungry child a stone instead? Or a snake when he asks for a fish? No father you would trust.

beats.speaker: jesus
beats.text: If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father which is in heaven give good things to them that ask him?

timing.text: If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father which is in heaven give good things to them that ask him?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: If flawed, tired, imperfect parents still love to give their kids good things — how much more does a perfect Father delight to give to you? Prayer is not twisting God's arm. It is a child asking a good Father who is glad to be asked.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: So the invitation is just this: ask. Not perfectly. Not impressively. Simply, honestly, like a child. The Father is not reluctant. He is leaning in, glad to hear your voice.

card.text: Ask, seek, knock. Jesus says your Father in heaven is far kinder than the best parent you can imagine, and glad to be asked. Is there something you have been afraid to ask him for?
